description: Tang Yuan are delightful Chinese glutinous rice balls, often served in a sweet soup. Their soft, chewy texture and delicious fillings make them a beloved dessert, especially during festivals. These comforting treats symbolize togetherness and completeness, bringing warmth to any gathering.

instructions.title: Prepare the Black Sesame Filling
instructions.text: In a food processor or with a mortar and pestle, grind the toasted black sesame seeds until fine. Mix with granulated sugar and melted lard or butter until a thick paste forms. Chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to firm up, then divide into small pea-sized portions and roll into tiny balls.

instructions.title: Make the Glutinous Rice Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, gradually add warm water to the glutinous rice flour, mixing with your hands or a spoon until a soft, pliable dough forms. The dough should not be too sticky or too dry. If it is too dry, add a tiny bit more water; if too sticky, add a little more flour.

instructions.title: Shape the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Take a small portion of the dough (about the size of a marble) and flatten it into a disc in your palm. Place one chilled black sesame filling ball in the center. Carefully cup the dough around the filling and seal it completely, then roll it gently between your palms to form a smooth, round ball. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ginger Soup
instructions.text: In a separate pot, combine 4 cups of water with ginger slices and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Keep warm over low heat.

instructions.title: Cook the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully drop the Tang Yuan into the boiling water, stirring gently to prevent them from sticking. Once they float to the surface, reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to cook for another 2-3 minutes until they are thoroughly cooked through and slightly translucent.

instructions.title: Serve the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Using a slotted spoon, carefully transfer the cooked Tang Yuan directly into bowls of the warm ginger soup. Serve immediately while hot. For extra flavor, you can garnish with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds or a few goji berries.

tips: For a perfectly smooth dough, ensure your warm water is not too hot, as it can cook the flour prematurely. Aim for lukewarm water.
If you dont have lard for the filling, unsalted butter or coconut oil can be used as a substitute, though the flavor will be slightly different.
Tang Yuan can be frozen raw on a floured tray until solid, then transferred to a freezer bag. Cook from frozen in boiling water, adding a few extra minutes to the cooking time.
